note: Plain-English definitions written by the project team for Agent 4 prompts. Not legal definitions.

terms.definition: To pay you back for a covered loss so you end up in about the same financial position as before it happened.
The person or business the policy protects - in this report, your business.
The insurance company that pays valid claims under the policy.
The building and land your business uses, as named in the policy.
The part of the policy that lists your specific details, such as what is insured, the amounts and any extra cover you chose.
The amount you pay yourself towards each claim before the insurer pays the rest.
Another word for excess: the part of each claim you pay yourself.
The maximum amount the insurer will pay for a type of loss.
Something the policy says it will not pay for.
Extra cover added to the basic policy, often only if it is shown in your schedule.
A written change to the policy that adds, removes or alters cover.
An event that can cause loss or damage, such as fire, storm or theft.
The income your business loses when it cannot trade normally, as worked out under the policy.
Cover for lost income and extra costs while your business cannot operate after damage.
The longest time after a loss for which lost income will be paid.
Getting into the premises by force, leaving visible damage such as broken locks or windows.
The dates between which the policy is active.
Your legal responsibility to pay for injury or damage you cause to other people or their property.
Someone other than you or the insurer, such as a customer or member of the public.
A request to the insurer to pay for a loss.
A rule in the policy you must follow for a claim to be paid, such as keeping locks and alarms working.
The form you filled in when applying for insurance; wrong answers on it can affect claims.
